    <h1>Alcohol Consumption and Cardiovascular Disease</h1>
    <p>
      Alcohol is another major behavioral exposure linked to cardiovascular disease. It is associated with higher blood pressure, arrhythmia, and increased risk of heart disease and stroke.
    </p>
  </header>

  <section class="story-section" aria-labelledby="alcohol-heading">

        <h3>474,000</h3>

      <article class="smoking-stat">

        <p>worldwide deaths from all causes attributable to alcohol in 2019</p>
      </article>

        <p>diseases and injuries associated with harmful alcohol use</p>
      </article>

    <p class="smoking-process">Alcohol consumption <span aria-hidden="true">→</span> increased blood pressure <span aria-hidden="true">→</span> cardiovascular damage <span aria-hidden="true">→</span> higher risk of heart disease or stroke</p>

    <p class="smoking-note">
      Alcohol use contributes to hypertension, arrhythmia, and coronary disease. It is an important behavioral predictor to compare across countries and over time, alongside smoking and inactivity.
